title: The Secret Agent
author: Joseph Conrad
description: Built around a real event: the 1894 attempt to bomb the Greenwich Observatory. Conrad walks his anarchists across a London he names honestly, from Verloc's shabby shop in Soho to the Embassy in Belgravia, and the Observatory is still standing. The bomb, the park, and Greenwich are exact; the street names around the shop and the Embassy are invented, which is what the labels are for.

route.summary: The novel opens here, in the seedy shop of dubious wares that fronts Verloc's real trade as a paid informer. He lives over it with his wife Winnie, her mother, and her brother Stevie, and by the last chapters it is the scene of a murder.
route.note: Verloc keeps his shop on Brett Street, which Conrad invented, but he sites it in the grimy Soho of the 1890s, the quarter of the foreign anarchist clubs. The pin marks central Soho.

route.summary: Summoned to the Embassy, Verloc is dressed down by the First Secretary, Mr Vladimir, who orders him to provoke an outrage that will frighten England into cracking down on the anarchists it shelters. The target Vladimir chooses is Greenwich.
route.note: Conrad walks Verloc to No. 10 Chesham Square, past a wall marked No. 1 Chesham Square and a stray house from Porthill Street, all invented names dropped into the real Belgravia near Vauxhall Bridge Road. The pin marks Belgrave Square, the heart of the district he names.

route.summary: The plan miscarries: the bomb detonates early and destroys the man carrying it. Only later does the reader learn it was Stevie, Winnie's simple brother, whom Verloc had sent up the hill with the explosive. Conrad drew the scene straight from the 1894 Greenwich Bomb Outrage.
route.note: The bomb goes off in Greenwich Park, on the slope below the Observatory. The pin marks the north-west slope of Observatory Hill, where the real anarchist Martial Bourdin died in 1894, the outrage Conrad built the novel on.

route.summary: The Observatory on the prime meridian is the outrage's target, chosen by Vladimir precisely because an attack on astronomy is senseless enough to terrify. Chief Inspector Heat reconstructs the last hundred yards to its walls, where the bomb went off before it could be laid.

To lighten the household after Verloc's troubles, Winnie's mother has herself admitted to a charity almshouse and leaves in a jolting cab, a self-sacrifice Winnie watches without fully grasping. It is one of the quiet cruelties that set the tragedy in motion.
route.note: The almshouses are not named, but Conrad's charity founded by a wealthy innkeeper for the destitute widows of the trade, reached by cab into South London, matches the Licensed Victuallers' Benevolent Institution Asylum, now Caroline Gardens, on Asylum Road in Peckham, a real home for retired publicans' widows. The pin marks it.

route.summary: Having killed Verloc, Winnie falls in with the anarchist Ossipon, who means to put her on the Southampton boat train from Waterloo and flee to the Continent with her savings. It is the last stage before she vanishes, and drowns in the Channel.
